question: Three ropes are 1 m 54 cm, 3 m 8 cm and 3 m 74 cm long. They are to be cut into pieces all of the same length, with nothing left over. What is the least number of pieces?
solution: Fewest pieces means the longest piece: in cm the lengths are 154, 308, 374; HCF(154, 308, 374) = 22 cm. Pieces = 154 ÷ 22 + 308 ÷ 22 + 374 ÷ 22 = 7 + 14 + 17 = 38.

question: What is the smallest number which, when increased by 12, is exactly divisible by 7, 8, 12 and 34?

question: Find the least number which when divided by 8, 12, 28 and 42 leaves remainders 2, 6, 22 and 36 respectively.
solution: Each remainder is 6 less than its divisor: 8 − 2 = 6, 12 − 6 = 6, 28 − 22 = 6, 42 − 36 = 6. So the number + 6 is divisible by all of them: the least is LCM(8, 12, 28, 42) − 6 = 168 − 6 = 162.

question: The LCM of two numbers is 54 times their HCF, and the sum of the HCF and the LCM is 1485. If one of the numbers is 54, what is the other?
solution: HCF + 54 × HCF = 1485, so 55 × HCF = 1485 and HCF = 27; LCM = 54 × 27 = 1458. Other number = HCF × LCM ÷ 54 = 27 × 1458 ÷ 54 = 729.

question: Find the HCF of 3212 and 3431 by the division method.
solution: Divide the larger by the smaller, then the divisor by the remainder, until the remainder is 0: 3431 = 1 × 3212 + 219; 3212 = 14 × 219 + 146; 219 = 1 × 146 + 73; 146 = 2 × 73 + 0. The last divisor, 73, is the HCF.

question: Bricks measuring 20 cm × 10 cm × 8 cm are stacked to make a solid cube. What is the least number of bricks needed?
solution: The side of the cube must be a multiple of each edge: the least is LCM(20, 10, 8) = 40 cm. Bricks = (40 ÷ 20) × (40 ÷ 10) × (40 ÷ 8) = 2 × 4 × 5 = 40.

question: Four bells start ringing together and ring at intervals of 16, 30, 36 and 40 seconds respectively. How many times will they ring together in 1 hour, not counting the time they start?

question: What is the HCF of 200, 400, 560 and 720?
solution: 200 = 2³ × 5², 400 = 2⁴ × 5², 560 = 2⁴ × 5 × 7, 720 = 2⁴ × 3² × 5. Only the primes common to all 4 numbers count, each with its lowest power: 2³ × 5 = 40. (200 and 400 alone have HCF 200, but 560 or 720 does not share all of it.)

question: Two gear wheels with 33 and 42 teeth turn together. A marked tooth of each is touching now. After how many complete turns of the smaller wheel will the two marked teeth touch again?

solution: The cube's edge must divide all three edges: the largest is HCF(60, 48, 30) = 6 cm. Cubes = (60 ÷ 6) × (48 ÷ 6) × (30 ÷ 6) = 10 × 8 × 5 = 400.

question: Three numbers are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 and their LCM is 330. What is their HCF?

question: What is the HCF of 225, 300, 350 and 375?
solution: 225 = 3² × 5², 300 = 2² × 3 × 5², 350 = 2 × 5² × 7, 375 = 3 × 5³. Only the primes common to all 4 numbers count, each with its lowest power: 5² = 25. (225 and 300 alone have HCF 75, but 350 or 375 does not share all of it.)

question: Four bells ring at intervals of 8, 12, 20 and 55 seconds respectively. If they ring together at 2:00:00 PM, at what time will they next ring together?
solution: LCM(8, 12, 20, 55) = 1320 seconds = 22 minutes. 2:00:00 PM + 22 minutes = 2:22:00 PM.

question: Find the HCF of 3/20, 9/8 and 15/16.

question: A shopkeeper has 297 litres, 594 litres and 693 litres of three kinds of juice. He fills them, without mixing, into tins of one size so that every tin is full. What is the least number of tins he needs?
solution: Fewest tins means the biggest tin: HCF(297, 594, 693) = 99 litres. Tins = 297 ÷ 99 + 594 ÷ 99 + 693 ÷ 99 = 3 + 6 + 7 = 16.

question: Two gear wheels with 20 and 48 teeth turn together. A marked tooth of each is touching now. After how many complete turns of the smaller wheel will the two marked teeth touch again?
solution: They meet again when the number of teeth passed is a multiple of both 20 and 48: LCM(20, 48) = 240 teeth. The smaller wheel then makes 240 ÷ 20 = 12 turns.

question: Find the least number which when divided by 15, 21, 33 and 44 leaves remainders 13, 19, 31 and 42 respectively.
solution: Each remainder is 2 less than its divisor: 15 − 13 = 2, 21 − 19 = 2, 33 − 31 = 2, 44 − 42 = 2. So the number + 2 is divisible by all of them: the least is LCM(15, 21, 33, 44) − 2 = 4620 − 2 = 4618.

question: Four bells start ringing together and ring at intervals of 20, 24, 30 and 36 seconds respectively. How many times will they ring together in 3 hours, counting the time they start?
solution: LCM(20, 24, 30, 36) = 360 seconds, so they ring together every 6 minutes. In 3 hours = 10800 seconds that is 10800 ÷ 360 = 30 times after the start, and 1 more at the start: 31.

question: A room is 5 m 44 cm long and 5 m 28 cm wide. Its floor is to be covered with square tiles, all of the same size, without cutting any tile. What is the least number of tiles needed?
solution: Fewest tiles means the largest tile: in cm the floor is 544 × 528; HCF(544, 528) = 16 cm. Tiles = (544 ÷ 16) × (528 ÷ 16) = 34 × 33 = 1122.

question: Find the greatest 5-digit number which is exactly divisible by 8, 13, 14 and 21.
solution: LCM(8, 13, 14, 21) = 2184. The greatest 5-digit number is 99999; 99999 ÷ 2184 leaves 1719, so the greatest multiple of 2184 is 99999 − 1719 = 98280. The answer is 98280.

question: The HCF of two numbers is 29 and their LCM is 1653. How many such pairs of numbers are possible?
solution: Let the numbers be 29a and 29b with a, b co-prime: their LCM is 29ab = 1653, so ab = 57. Co-prime pairs with product 57: (1, 57), (3, 19) - 2 pairs.

question: How many common factors do 952 and 2108 have?
solution: The common factors of two numbers are the factors of their HCF. HCF(952, 2108) = 68 = 2² × 17, whose factors are 1, 2, 4, 17, 34, 68: 6 in all (1 and 68 included).
